msg: Hola, buen día. Somos un grupo de 7 amigas de Bogotá. Tres ya tenemos el Open Water, dos quieren probar el minicurso y dos prefieren snorkel. ¿Cuánto saldría por persona saliendo desde Cartagena y hay descuento por grupo?
reply:
¡Hola! 🪸 Soy *Coral*, de *Diving Planet* — buceamos todo el año en las Islas del Rosario, saliendo desde Cartagena o desde las propias islas. 🌊

¡Buen día! ¡Qué plan tan bacano, 7 amigas juntas en las Islas del Rosario! 🌊

Sí se puede combinar todo en un mismo tour: las tres certificadas hacen sus inmersiones, las dos del minicurso arrancan con la parte teórica y práctica, y las dos del snorkel van a su zona. Si el grupo es pequeño van juntas en la misma lancha; si no, se dividen por actividad. Todo el mundo comparte el día y el almuerzo. 🐠

Sobre el descuento: sí, por ser 7 personas les aplica el 10% de grupo, que se suma al 10% de reservar online (20% en total). Eso sí, hay que pedirlo al equipo **antes de pagar**, porque no se aplica automático y después no se puede devolver. Aplica a buceo recreativo, minicurso y snorkel.

Te dejo los precios por persona saliendo desde Cartagena justo a continuación 👇

*Precios por persona* (online · normal):
• Minicurso de Buceo: 655.000 COP · 727.000 COP
• Tour de Snorkeling: 448.000 COP · 497.000 COP

No hay descuento ni tarifa especial por ser colombiano: el precio es el mismo, solo cambia la moneda (COP).

¿Quieres que te ayude a armar la reserva para las 7?

msg: Hello. My wife and I arrive on a cruise ship in Cartagena on March 3rd, docking at 7:00 am and we must be back on board by 5:00 pm. We would both like to snorkel. Is that doable? We are from Canada.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Snorkeling in the Rosario Islands is a beautiful plan — the reefs there are full of life and perfect for a relaxed day in the water. 🤿

And yes, it fits your schedule. Here's how the day looks from Cartagena:

- Meeting point: Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. (5 minutes from the historic center; no hotel pick-up from Cartagena, you get to the dock on your own)
- Speedboat to the Rosario Islands (about 1 hour)
- Gear setup, then 2 guided snorkeling sessions with a surface interval
- Lunch at the hotel facilities
- Return to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m., arriving around 4:15 p.m. — so you'd be back well before your 5:00 p.m. boarding time

The Snorkeling Tour is 126 USD per person online (140 USD regular), and since you're international guests the price is in USD. Minimum age is 6, no certification needed, and gear is included.

One thing to keep in mind: the online booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before, so for March 3rd it's best to book ahead of time.

So, would you leave *from Cartagena* (Muelle de la Bodeguita)? 🚤

msg: I see, thanks. Is there anything shorter we could do that gets us back by 3 pm? Or could we go from the islands somehow?
reply:
Good news — the snorkeling itself is a shorter day than the Cartagena version, and it fits your 3:00 p.m. comfortably. 🤿

If you're already on the Rosario Islands, we pick you up at your hotel between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (if your hotel has boat access; in some cases the boat comes right to the hotel, in others we point you to the nearest dock). Then gear setup at our base, 2 snorkeling sessions on the reefs with a surface interval, and you're back at your hotel around 12:00–1:00 p.m. — well before 3:00 p.m. 🌊

The Snorkeling Tour from the islands is 45 USD per person online (50 USD regular), lunch not included, gear included, no certification needed.

One note: pick-up times are fixed, so they can't be moved earlier or later.

Diving Planet policies:
- Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). The refresher is also 18 hours: it is for certified divers, even though it is booked as the mini course. The hours count from the last dive, not from the return to Cartagena. The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.
- If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
- For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
- Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, at 8:00 AM. Departing from Cartagena there is no hotel pick-up: each person gets to the dock on their own (ground transportation to the dock is not included).
- By booking you accept our terms and conditions, cancellation policy, and data treatment. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Date changes are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Changes to the number of people on a booking you already made are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Colombians (anyone with Colombian nationality, holding a Colombian cédula or passport, wherever they live; also dual nationals when one nationality is Colombian) and residents of Colombia (holders of a cédula de extranjería, a resident ID; living in Colombia without one is not enough) pay in Colombian pesos (COP). Saying they are Colombian or from a Colombian city ("I'm from Cali") already says it; what is not enough is only having been born there while living abroad: then ask whether they hold Colombian nationality or a cédula de extranjería. All other international clients pay in US dollars (USD). A group does not pay in parts: if the same booking mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group pays in US dollars (USD), residents and Colombians included. A Colombian together with someone who holds a cédula de extranjería, wherever they are from, is not a mixed group: both pay in pesos (COP). The price is the same: only the currency changes (there is no discount for being Colombian).
- If the group mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group booking is paid in US dollars (USD), at the same equivalent price. Someone with a cédula de extranjería does not count as a foreigner, wherever they are from. There is no different price for being Colombian.
- If you are already on the Rosario Islands, we coordinate pick-up and drop-off from hotels with maritime access. In some cases the boat arrives directly at the hotel; in others we indicate the nearest dock or meeting point.
- These plans have different prices because they do not include transport from Cartagena or lunch.
- Pick-up is only on the Rosario Islands: Barú (including Playa Blanca, which is on Barú) is not part of the islands and we do not operate or pick up there; guests staying in Barú depart from Cartagena (Muelle de la Bodeguita).
- It depends on the activity: snorkeling from 6 years old; Bubble Makers from 8 to 10 years old (pool mini-course and very shallow water practice, max 2 meters); the dive mini-course and the Open Water course from 10 years old; the Advanced course and the Rescue course from 12. Minors must be accompanied by a demonstrable parent or responsible relative.
- The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
- If you are a certified diver, there are no additional medical restrictions; your liability waiver is the certified-diver one: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). For the refresher day this one is not used: use the course medical form.
- Bringing or drinking alcohol on the boat or during the activity is not allowed, and no alcohol or other substances may be consumed before diving. You must be in good physical condition.
- The booking system on our website. It automatically closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you can no longer book for the next day, and you still book on the website for the next available day.
- To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
- From Cartagena: departure at 8:00 a.m. from Muelle de la Bodeguita and return at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.). From the islands: hotel pick-up between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (8:00 a.m. for specialties and 7:30 a.m. on day 2 of some courses). Daytime activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m. (see the activity schedule). Night diving: in the evening (pick-up around 5:30 p.m., back around 7:30 p.m.). Online booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before; after that, you book on the website for the next available day.
- We only close on December 25 and January 1. The rest of the year we operate every day, including public holidays, except for suspension due to adverse weather conditions.
- The tour includes water all day, coconut candy between dives, and lunch (rice with chicken or rice with vegetables). The menu is always the same, it does not change by day/supplier. If the guest has a food allergy, they must inform us before the tour. In multi-day packages departing from Cartagena, lunch is included on the first day only; plans for guests already on the islands do not include lunch.
- Photos and videos are not offered proactively or included in the price. The instructor may take them voluntarily and delivers them by the next day at the latest. - The 3, 4, 5, 7 and 9 dive packages are exclusively for certified divers with a minimum Open Water level. They are not available for uncertified beginners.
- Two-day courses (Open Water, Referral Course, Advanced, Rescue and Mindful Diving) require accommodation on the islands: at least one night, the night of day 1 (there is no return to Cartagena on day 1). There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel. The same goes for multi-day dive packages (4, 5, 7 and 9 dives): you stay on the islands, and accommodation, which is not included, is booked directly with the hotel.
- Private services and closed groups are available, with no fixed price (it depends on the group and the date). A member of our team prepares the quote and coordinates an available instructor for the date.
- Through DIVE TO HEAL, more than 360 people with disabilities have been served. Accepted conditions include: hearing impairment (deaf), visual impairment (blind), reduced mobility (wheelchair), Down Syndrome, Cerebral Palsy, and Autism (depending on level and assessment). All instructors are trained in adaptive diving. Advance notice is recommended. The limitation is the presence of additional medical conditions that contraindicate diving.
- If you're already on the Rosario Islands and your hotel has maritime access, boat pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge.
- We dive in the Rosario Islands, inside the Corales del Rosario y San Bernardo National Natural Park, about 45-60 minutes by boat from Cartagena.
- All daytime activities (dive trips, mini-course, snorkeling, courses and each day of the packages) end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., followed by lunch. Booking for the SAME day is no longer possible (trips leave in the morning and the website closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before): you book for the next available day.
- Each person can bring one backpack or bag on the boat. If the guest needs to bring a suitcase, it has to be arranged with a member of our team. If they prefer not to take it, we can store the suitcase at our office in Cartagena.
- What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.
- At our base on the island there are lockers where you can leave your things (clothes, phone, wallet) while you dive or snorkel.
- There is no minimum number of people: every activity runs even for a single person.
- Activities and courses are taught in Spanish and English. If a participant speaks neither language, they can come with someone who interprets for them, but instruction is still given in Spanish or English.
- Bookings are made on our website, through each activity's link (with the 10% online discount). The system closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you still book on the website, for the next available day. Plans with no booking link (the 3- and 4-dive packages, the 9-dive package from the islands, the 1-dive trip from the islands, Bubble Makers, Divemaster and the private service) are booked by an advisor in this chat.
- Besides the insurance form, each diver fills in a liability waiver. Our team sends it to you to complete (certified divers: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish)), and the confirmation email reminds you if you have not done it yet.
- The mini-course is a one-day try-dive, an introduction to diving: it does not certify, does not count as part of any PADI course and requires nothing from PADI beforehand (no PADI account or PADI online course). It is the same departing from Cartagena or already on the islands: there is no online or emailed theory; the theory is done there, on the day, along with pool practice and 1 ocean dive with an instructor.
- International clients pay 100% by card on the website; with a foreign card the passport is used as the ID document.
- Colombians and residents of Colombia (including holders of a cédula de extranjería) pay in pesos and do not use the website booking link: a team advisor always closes the booking in this chat and sends them the link, QR code or Llave to pay 100% online or a 50% deposit, and the other 50% on the day of the activity, by card or cash. The 50% deposit option is only for them. Nobody pays 100% at the dock without booking online.
- If you leave the next day around noon: from the Rosario Islands it is very tight (pickup is between 9:30 and 9:45 and the activity ends around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), so it is best to confirm it with a team advisor; departing from Cartagena it does not fit (the boat returns at 3:00 p.m. and arrives around 4:15 p.m.). - In groups combining diving and snorkeling, snorkeling takes place in a different area from the dive sites. If there are few people everyone goes on the same boat; otherwise the group is split by activity.
- Besides our base (Hotel San Pedro de Majagua and Hotel Cocoliso, on Isla Grande), other hotels in the area with maritime access are Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras and Pao Pao. Accommodation is not included: it is booked directly with the hotel.
- To book an activity departing from the islands, the customer must already have their hotel and tell us which one: pickup is arranged there. If they booked the activity first, the hotel could be cancelled, it could be full, they could forget to tell us or end up departing from Cartagena. If they stay in a house, an Airbnb or a hotel not on our list, they tell us the name and an advisor confirms the pickup before they book and pay: they do not book until then.
- Returning to Cartagena on a different date from the plan is not included. If the guest wants to stay longer on the islands and come back with us another day, a member of our team arranges it (space on the boat, etc.).
- Departure and pickup times are fixed: they cannot be moved earlier or later. If you need an adjustment, a team advisor reviews it.
- Cancellations due to bad weather are unlikely because the Rosario Islands are in sheltered waters. - Scuba diving is not possible during pregnancy: no mini-course, no dive trips and no courses (DAN and obstetricians advise against it for the whole pregnancy). Surface snorkeling is possible, with her doctor's approval. Whoever comes with her can dive as usual.
- If you get seasick on the boat (the ride to the islands is about 1 hour by speedboat): have a light breakfast before leaving and consider seasickness tablets. If you take any medication, ask your doctor whether you can dive with it.
- We do issue invoices (also to companies). An advisor from our team coordinates the invoice details with the customer.
- There is no maximum age for diving: an older person can dive with the same medical form as everyone else.
- We carry oxygen and a first-aid kit on board, with trained staff, and there is an emergency protocol.
- Groups are small and follow PADI safety standards for each activity.
- The boat is a regular speedboat with no bathroom. On the islands we use the facilities of the hotel where lunch is served: that is where you change, use the bathroom and shower.
- Diving Planet has no parking of its own; there are public car parks in the old town area, and the easiest way to reach the pier is by taxi.
- There is no gift card, but you can book in someone else's name; the date and details are arranged with an advisor.
- Smoking is not allowed on the boat.
- Pets are not allowed on the boat: we go to a National Natural Park.
- Babies and young children who are not yet old enough for any activity (snorkeling starts at 6) can ride the boat with their parents at any age, and they ride free.
- You can bring your own camera on the dives or snorkeling, at your own risk. Diving Planet does not rent cameras.

msg: Hi, we're two Dutch divers, both Rescue Divers, in Cartagena from the 10th to the 16th. We bring our own full gear. We want to dive on three separate days from Cartagena, coming back to the city each night. What's the best price for us?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Perfect! Three separate days of diving from Cartagena is a great plan — you'll get to see different sites around the Rosario Islands and still sleep in the city each night. 🌊

For that pattern, the plan that fits is **Fun Dives – 2 dives (1 day)**, booked once for each of your three days. It's a full-day trip with the boat Cartagena–Islands–Cartagena included, lunch included, and gear included. Since you're both certified, you're all set to dive.

Two things worth knowing:
- From Cartagena the minimum is 2 dives per trip, so each of your three days would be a 2-dive day.
- Since you're bringing your **complete** gear (regulator, BCD, wetsuit, mask, fins), the 5% own-equipment discount applies — and it stacks with the 10% online discount.

I'm leaving the per-person prices below. You can pick your three dates and the number of people right here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/salidas-de-buceo/1?language=en

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Fun Dives - 2 dives (1 day): 178 USD · 197 USD
• 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive): 287 USD · 319 USD
• 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 316 USD · 351 USD

Would you like help getting the three days set up?

msg: Ciao! Siamo due amici italiani, vorremmo fare un'immersione con il minicorso, non abbiamo mai fatto immersioni. Quanto costa e cosa è incluso?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Ciao! What a great plan for a first dive — the Dive Mini Course is exactly the experience for people who have never dived before, and the Rosario Islands are a beautiful place to try it. 🌊

It's a one-day introduction: theory and pool practice with an instructor, then one open-water dive on the reef. No prior experience or certification needed, and nothing to study online beforehand — the theory is done there on the day.

What's included depends on where you'd start from:

**From Cartagena:** National Park entrance fee, dive insurance, boat transport Cartagena–Islands–Cartagena, pool training + 1 ocean dive with a PADI instructor, diving equipment, lunch, and the eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL. Meeting point is Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m., back in Cartagena around 4:15 p.m. (ground transport to the dock isn't included).

**If you're already on the Rosario Islands:** hotel pick-up if your hotel has boat access, dive insurance, diving equipment, and a PADI professional with you throughout. These plans don't include transport from Cartagena or lunch.

I'm leaving the prices per person below for you.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
*From Cartagena* — boat from Muelle de la Bodeguita · lunch included
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD
*Already on the Rosario Islands* — pickup at your hotel if it has boat access · no lunch
• Dive Mini Course: 134 USD · 149 USD

Would you leave *from Cartagena* or are you already *on the Rosario Islands*? Then I'll give you the exact plan. 🌊

msg: Ok from Cartagena. We are from Milan, the 12th of May. Is lunch vegetarian possible? And what do we have to bring?
reply:
Perfect, from Cartagena it is! 🌊 And yes — vegetarian lunch is no problem at all.

**Lunch:** the menu is rice with chicken or rice with vegetables, and vegetarians (and vegans or celiacs) get the rice with vegetables. If either of you has a food allergy, just let us know before the tour so it can be managed. You're also welcome to bring your own food if you prefer.

**What to bring:** swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. The diving equipment is included in the mini-course, so no need to bring any gear. 🐠

A couple of practical notes for the day:
- Meeting point: Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m., 5 minutes from the historic center. There's no hotel pick-up from Cartagena, so you get to the dock on your own.
- Estimated return to Cartagena: around 4:15 p.m.
- There's no theory to study beforehand — it's done there on the day with the instructor.
- The medical form is required for the mini-course, and it's in Spanish: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol
- After diving, wait at least 12 hours before flying.

Would you like me to help you set up the booking for the 12th of May?

msg: Hi, my flight lands in Cartagena on Saturday at 11:30 am and I leave on Sunday at 8 pm. I'm PADI Advanced, last dive 3 months ago. Could I fit in some diving? I'm from the UK.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Great that you're thinking about diving with us — the Rosario Islands are beautiful and you'd love it. Let me be straight with you on the timing, though.

After recreational diving you need to wait at least 18 hours before flying, counted from your last dive. With your Sunday 8 pm flight, your last dive would have to be on Saturday at the latest — a dive on Sunday doesn't work, even though the boat gets back in the afternoon.

The tricky part is Saturday: your flight lands at 11:30 am, and our Cartagena trips leave at 8:00 am and return around 4:15 pm, so Saturday morning is already gone by the time you land.

So with those two days, fitting in a dive trip from Cartagena is very tight. If you're staying on the Rosario Islands, it could be different — there we can pick you up at your hotel if it has boat access, and the schedule is shorter.

There is always availability: we operate every day, including public holidays, except December 25 and January 1; if sea conditions are not safe, the trip is rescheduled.

Would you like me to connect you with a team advisor to look at the options for your exact dates?

msg: Wait, I fly on Sunday at 8 pm. So can I dive on Sunday morning and still fly that night?
reply:
After recreational diving you need to wait at least 18 hours before flying, counted from your last dive. So if your last dive is a daytime one on Sunday (ending around 12:00–1:00 p.m.), you could fly from about 7:00 a.m. on Monday — not Sunday night.

For a certified diver, a flight on the same day as the dive never works, whatever the time, even at night. The boat being back before your flight doesn't change that. With a Sunday 8 pm flight, your last dive would have to be on Saturday at the latest.

And Saturday is the tight one: your flight lands at 11:30 am, while our Cartagena trips leave at 8:00 am and return around 4:15 pm — so Saturday morning is already gone by the time you land. If you're staying on the Rosario Islands, the schedule is shorter (pickup 9:30–9:45 am, back around 12:00–1:00 pm), which could make Saturday more feasible.

Would you leave *from Cartagena* or are you already *on the Rosario Islands*? Then I'll give you the exact plan. 🌊

Other ways to ask: Can I fly the same day I dive? / What's the minimum time between diving and flying?
Answer: Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.

msg: Hello, I have my Advanced and 40 logged dives, and I'd like to do the Rescue Diver course. Do I need EFR? How many days and how much? I'm from France and I'm already staying on Isla Grande at Cocoliso.
reply:

Perfect! The Rescue Diver course is a great next step — it's one of the most rewarding courses, and with your Advanced and 40 dives you're in a great spot for it. 🌊

msg: Solo yo. ¿A qué hora me recogerían en el Cocoliso y tengo que llevar algo? Gracias.
reply:
En Cocoliso te recogen entre las 9:30 y las 9:45, y el regreso al hotel es hacia las 12:00-13:00. La recogida y el regreso en lancha están incluidos sin cargo adicional. 🐠

Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo va incluido. Y no olvides tu carnet de buceo (puedes enviarnos una foto antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad). También hay que completar el formato del seguro que llega en el correo de confirmación.

También necesitas:
• Estar listo a las 9:30 en tu hotel
• Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh; los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) los revisa un asesor del equipo. Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente. El refresher es el minicurso (piscina y una inmersión con instructor) y ocupa su propio día: ese mismo día no se hace la salida de buceo. Quien viene varios días hace el refresher el primero y bucea los demás.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 18 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.

¿Han pasado *más de 2 años* desde tu última inmersión?

msg: Hi there! We're a family from Canada staying in Cartagena next month. My wife and I are both Advanced Open Water divers, and we have two kids, aged 11 and 7. What could each of us do on a day trip from Cartagena, and how much would it cost?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

What a great family plan! A day out in the Rosario Islands works beautifully with those ages — warm water, a beautiful reef and something for everyone. 🌊

Here's how a day trip from Cartagena could look for each of you:

**You and your wife (Advanced certified):** the *Fun Dives – 2 dives* day trip — two guided reef dives, boat from Cartagena and back the same day, lunch included. If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher (booked as the Dive Mini Course) is normally required first, on its own day.

**Your 11-year-old:** can do the *Dive Mini Course* (pool session + 1 ocean dive with an instructor, no experience needed) or the *Snorkeling Tour*. Both are same-day round trips from Cartagena with lunch included.

**Your 7-year-old:** the *Snorkeling Tour* — the reef from the surface, minimum age 6, gear and lunch included. Diving programmes start at 8 (Bubble Makers), so snorkeling is the option at 7.

One note: minors need to be accompanied by a responsible adult during their activity.

I'm leaving the prices per person for each plan just below.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Fun Dives - 2 dives (1 day): 178 USD · 197 USD
• Snorkeling Tour: 126 USD · 140 USD
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

Would you like me to help you put the day together, or send you the booking links for the plans you like?

Good news — your daughter has a lovely option! 🌊 At 7 she can do the *Snorkeling Tour*: she goes in the water with the group and enjoys the reef from the surface, with gear included. So she's not stuck on the boat at all. And since she's a minor, one of you accompanies her in the water — which works out nicely, as you can take turns diving and snorkeling.

For your 11-year-old, no problem at all that he's never dived: the *Dive Mini Course* is made exactly for that — a first pool session and a shallow ocean dive with an instructor, no certification needed. If he loves it, the *Open Water* course is the natural next step (from age 10).

So a day could look like: you and your wife on the *Fun Dives – 2 dives*, your son on the *Dive Mini Course*, and your daughter snorkeling with one of you alongside. 🐠

Shall we go for the *2-dive trip*, a *multi-day package* or an *advanced course*? 🌊

msg: That's better, thank you. So my wife and I would do the 2 dives, our son the mini course and our daughter the snorkeling. If both of us are diving, who stays with our daughter while she's snorkeling, given she has to be accompanied? And do we all go on the same boat?
reply:
Good question — and it's worth planning that bit. 🌊

The snorkeling happens in a different area from the dive sites, and the snorkeling group goes with its own guide. Since your daughter is a minor, one of you needs to be with her in the water — so the practical way is to take turns: one of you dives while the other snorkels with her, then you swap. That way you both get your two dives and she's always accompanied. Your son, meanwhile, does his theory and pool practice with the instructor before his open water dive.

As for the boat: in groups that combine diving and snorkeling, if there are few people everyone goes together on the same boat; if the group is larger, they split by activity. Either way you all head out together from Cartagena and come back the same day.

Has it been *more than 2 years* since any diver in the group last dived?

msg: Good afternoon. I am from Germany and I hold an Open Water certification, although I have not dived for three years. I am staying in Getsemaní and I would like to dive next Wednesday. My flight home leaves on Thursday at 22:00. Is this possible, and what would you recommend?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Good afternoon! Diving the Rosario Islands is a beautiful plan, and your timing works out nicely. 🌊

Since it's been three years since your last dive, the best fit is our **Refresher** (booked as the Dive Mini Course): a review for certified divers with more than 2 years without diving.

On the flight: after recreational diving you need to wait at least 18 hours before flying, and the refresher counts as 18 hours too. With a daytime dive, activities end around 12:00–1:00 p.m., so you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day. Your Thursday 22:00 flight is well after that, so diving on Wednesday is fine. ✈️

A couple of practical notes:
- Departure is at 8:00 a.m. from Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, and the boat returns to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.).
- Please bring your certification card (a photo beforehand works too, or show it on the day).
- To book for next Wednesday, do it before 4:30 p.m. on Tuesday, when the online system closes.

You can pick your date and pay here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=en

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 316 USD · 351 USD
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

There is always availability: we operate every day, including public holidays, except December 25 and January 1; if sea conditions are not safe, the trip is rescheduled.

Would you like me to help you get the booking set up?

The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.
- If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
- For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
- Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, at 8:00 AM. Departing from Cartagena there is no hotel pick-up: each person gets to the dock on their own (ground transportation to the dock is not included).

- Date changes are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Changes to the number of people on a booking you already made are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Colombians (anyone with Colombian nationality, holding a Colombian cédula or passport, wherever they live; also dual nationals when one nationality is Colombian) and residents of Colombia (holders of a cédula de extranjería, a resident ID; living in Colombia without one is not enough) pay in Colombian pesos (COP). Saying they are Colombian or from a Colombian city ("I'm from Cali") already says it; what is not enough is only having been born there while living abroad: then ask whether they hold Colombian nationality or a cédula de extranjería. All other international clients pay in US dollars (USD). A group does not pay in parts: if the same booking mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group pays in US dollars (USD), residents and Colombians included. A Colombian together with someone who holds a cédula de extranjería, wherever they are from, is not a mixed group: both pay in pesos (COP). The price is the same: only the currency changes (there is no discount for being Colombian).
- If the group mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group booking is paid in US dollars (USD), at the same equivalent price. Someone with a cédula de extranjería does not count as a foreigner, wherever they are from. There is no different price for being Colombian.
- If you are already on the Rosario Islands, we coordinate pick-up and drop-off from hotels with maritime access. In some cases the boat arrives directly at the hotel; in others we indicate the nearest dock or meeting point.
- These plans have different prices because they do not include transport from Cartagena or lunch.
- Pick-up is only on the Rosario Islands: Barú (including Playa Blanca, which is on Barú) is not part of the islands and we do not operate or pick up there; guests staying in Barú depart from Cartagena (Muelle de la Bodeguita).
- It depends on the activity: snorkeling from 6 years old; Bubble Makers from 8 to 10 years old (pool mini-course and very shallow water practice, max 2 meters); the dive mini-course and the Open Water course from 10 years old; the Advanced course and the Rescue course from 12. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
- If you are a certified diver, there are no additional medical restrictions; your liability waiver is the certified-diver one: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). For the refresher day this one is not used: use the course medical form.
- Bringing or drinking alcohol on the boat or during the activity is not allowed, and no alcohol or other substances may be consumed before diving. You must be in good physical condition.
- The booking system on our website. It automatically closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you can no longer book for the next day, and you still book on the website for the next available day.
- To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.

The same goes for multi-day dive packages (4, 5, 7 and 9 dives): you stay on the islands, and accommodation, which is not included, is booked directly with the hotel.
- Private services and closed groups are available, with no fixed price (it depends on the group and the date). A member of our team prepares the quote and coordinates an available instructor for the date.
- Through DIVE TO HEAL, more than 360 people with disabilities have been served. All instructors are trained in adaptive diving. Advance notice is recommended. The limitation is the presence of additional medical conditions that contraindicate diving.
- If you're already on the Rosario Islands and your hotel has maritime access, boat pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge.
- We dive in the Rosario Islands, inside the Corales del Rosario y San Bernardo National Natural Park, about 45-60 minutes by boat from Cartagena.

- There is no minimum number of people: every activity runs even for a single person.

- Bookings are made on our website, through each activity's link (with the 10% online discount). - Colombians and residents of Colombia (including holders of a cédula de extranjería) pay in pesos and do not use the website booking link: a team advisor always closes the booking in this chat and sends them the link, QR code or Llave to pay 100% online or a 50% deposit, and the other 50% on the day of the activity, by card or cash. - Besides our base (Hotel San Pedro de Majagua and Hotel Cocoliso, on Isla Grande), other hotels in the area with maritime access are Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras and Pao Pao. Accommodation is not included: it is booked directly with the hotel.
- To book an activity departing from the islands, the customer must already have their hotel and tell us which one: pickup is arranged there. If they booked the activity first, the hotel could be cancelled, it could be full, they could forget to tell us or end up departing from Cartagena. If they stay in a house, an Airbnb or a hotel not on our list, they tell us the name and an advisor confirms the pickup before they book and pay: they do not book until then.
- Returning to Cartagena on a different date from the plan is not included. If the guest wants to stay longer on the islands and come back with us another day, a member of our team arranges it (space on the boat, etc.).
- Departure and pickup times are fixed: they cannot be moved earlier or later. If you need an adjustment, a team advisor reviews it.
- Cancellations due to bad weather are unlikely because the Rosario Islands are in sheltered waters. If rescheduling is not possible, you get a 100% refund. See the terms and conditions: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Scuba diving is not possible during pregnancy: no mini-course, no dive trips and no courses (DAN and obstetricians advise against it for the whole pregnancy). Surface snorkeling is possible, with her doctor's approval. Whoever comes with her can dive as usual.
- If you get seasick on the boat (the ride to the islands is about 1 hour by speedboat): have a light breakfast before leaving and consider seasickness tablets. If you take any medication, ask your doctor whether you can dive with it.
- We do issue invoices (also to companies). An advisor from our team coordinates the invoice details with the customer.
- There is no maximum age for diving: an older person can dive with the same medical form as everyone else.
- We carry oxygen and a first-aid kit on board, with trained staff, and there is an emergency protocol.
- Groups are small and follow PADI safety standards for each activity.
- The boat is a regular speedboat with no bathroom. On the islands we use the facilities of the hotel where lunch is served: that is where you change, use the bathroom and shower.
- Diving Planet has no parking of its own; there are public car parks in the old town area, and the easiest way to reach the pier is by taxi.
- There is no gift card, but you can book in someone else's name; the date and details are arranged with an advisor.
- Smoking is not allowed on the boat.
- Pets are not allowed on the boat: we go to a National Natural Park.
- Babies and young children who are not yet old enough for any activity (snorkeling starts at 6) can ride the boat with their parents at any age, and they ride free.
- You can bring your own camera on the dives or snorkeling, at your own risk. Diving Planet does not rent cameras.

msg: Thank you. What exactly does the refresher consist of? I would prefer to do proper dives on Wednesday: could I do a short review with the guide in the morning and then the 2 dives on the same day? I could also come on Tuesday if necessary.
reply:
The refresher can't be squeezed in before the dives on the same day — it takes its own full day. It's the mini course format: pool session with theory and confined-water practice, then 1 reef dive with a PADI instructor, all at our island base. So the review and the 2-dive trip can't be combined on Wednesday.

The good news is your Tuesday idea works perfectly. 🌊 You'd do the refresher on Tuesday, and then Wednesday you're free to do the **Fun Dives – 2 dives** (two different sites, 40–50 minutes each, lunch included). And your Thursday 22:00 flight is no problem: after Wednesday's daytime dives you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day.

Here's what the refresher day looks like:
- 8:00 a.m. at Muelle de la Bodeguita (5 min from the historic center)
- Speedboat to the Rosario Islands (about 1 hour)
- Welcome at our island base, equipment setup with instructor support
- Pool session: theory and confined-water practice
- 1 reef dive + surface interval
- Lunch at the hotel facilities
- Return to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.)

It includes the National Park entrance fee, mandatory dive insurance, boat transport, pool training + 1 ocean dive with a PADI instructor, equipment, lunch and our eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL. Not included: ground transport to the dock, photos/videos, tips, extra food, and return on a different date.

You can book the refresher here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=en
And the 2 dives here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/salidas-de-buceo/1?language=en

One thing to keep in mind: to book for Tuesday, do it before 4:30 p.m. on Monday, when the online system closes. And bring your certification card (a photo beforehand works too).

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Fun Dives - 2 dives (1 day): 178 USD · 197 USD
• Snorkeling Tour: 126 USD · 140 USD
• 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 316 USD · 351 USD
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

Other ways to ask: What does the Rescue Diver course involve and what are its benefits? / Why is it relevant to take the Rescue Diver course?
Answer: Rescue Diver is an advanced recreational course focused on prevention, emergency management, and diver rescue. It does not grant a professional level; the first professional level is Divemaster.

msg: Good, thank you. Two last questions: do you pick me up in Getsemaní or how do I reach the dock, and do I have to bring my certification card or fill in any forms for these two days?
reply:
There's no hotel pick-up from Getsemaní: you make your own way to the dock. The meeting point is **Muelle de la Bodeguita**, 5 minutes from the historic center, at **8:00 a.m.** — just ask for DIVING PLANET at entrance 3. Ground transport to the dock isn't included, but it's a short taxi or walk from Getsemaní. 🚤

On the card and forms:
- **Certification card:** yes, bring it both days. You can send a photo beforehand or just show it on the day.
- **Forms:** the insurance form comes in your booking confirmation email. For the refresher day you use the **course medical form** (even as a certified diver): https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (it's in Spanish). For the 2-dive day, the certified-diver liability waiver: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol

You'll also need:
• If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
• After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying
• Minimum age: 10 and over.
• For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
• What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.

The *refresher* is an instructor-led review before diving again: it is booked as the *Dive Mini Course* and costs *183 USD* per person who needs it. It uses the course medical form (even for certified divers; the link comes with the booking). Are you interested?

msg: Buenas tardes. Somos 6 amigos de Bogotá, todos certificados, y queremos hacer dos días de buceo saliendo desde Cartagena. ¿Tienen descuento de grupo? Dos de nosotros llevamos nuestro equipo completo: ¿hay descuento por eso y se suma al de grupo?
reply:
¡Hola! 🪸 Soy *Coral*, de *Diving Planet* — buceamos todo el año en las Islas del Rosario, saliendo desde Cartagena o desde las propias islas. 🌊

Qué bueno, 6 amigos certificados con dos días de buceo desde Cartagena — se van a gozar esos arrecifes. 🤿

Te cuento cómo funcionan los descuentos:

**Grupo (5 o más):** sí, 10% de descuento, que se suma al 10% online (20% total reservando online). Ojo: no se aplica automático, hay que pedirlo al equipo **antes de pagar**; si pagan sin pedirlo, ya no se puede aplicar después.

**Equipo propio:** 5% si traen el equipo COMPLETO (regulador, BCD, traje, máscara, aletas). Aplica solo a buceo recreativo y cursos PADI, y solo a quienes traen el equipo completo.

**¿Se suman?** El de equipo propio se suma al online, pero **no se suma al de grupo**. Es decir, cada uno se suma solo al 10% online, no entre ellos.

Para dos días de buceo desde Cartagena tienen dos opciones:
- **Paquete de 4 inmersiones (2 días, 4 diurnas):** 316 USD / 1.154.000 COP online (351 USD / 1.282.000 COP normal)
- **Paquete de 5 inmersiones (2 días, incluye nocturna):** 392 USD / 1.429.000 COP online (436 USD / 1.587.000 COP normal)

Ambos incluyen lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena, almuerzo el día 1, equipo y requieren dormir en las islas (alojamiento no incluido).

Como son colombianos, pagan en pesos (COP), al mismo precio online, y la reserva se las cierra un asesor por este chat.

¿Quieres que te pase con un asesor para aplicar el descuento de grupo y cuadrar las fechas?

msg: Hey! I'm an American diver, Advanced Open Water. I'm renting a house on Airbnb on Isla Grande next week, it's called Villa Marea. I'd like to do two dives. Can you pick me up there? How does that work?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Great choice — two dives around the Rosario Islands is a beautiful way to spend a day, and the reef here is full of life. 🌊

Since you're staying in a house (Airbnb) and not one of our base hotels, pick-up isn't automatically confirmed: you'd need to tell us the name of the house and a team advisor confirms the pick-up logistics before you book and pay. If the house has maritime access, boat pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge; if not, we'd indicate the nearest dock or meeting point.

For the 2-dive day, if you're already on the islands:
- Pick-up at your place between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (if it has boat access)
- Transfer to our base and gear set-up
- 2 open-water dives + surface interval at the base
- Back at your place around 12:00–1:00 p.m.

Price for Fun Dives – 2 dives (already on the islands): 124 USD / 440.000 COP online per person (138 USD / 489.000 COP regular). Lunch is not included on the island version. Certification required, and gear is included.

Would you like me to connect you with a team advisor so they can confirm the pick-up at Villa Marea before you book?

msg: Gracias. Nos interesa el minicurso, para los dos. ¿A qué profundidad se baja? Y mi esposa pregunta si hace falta saber nadar muy bien, porque ella nada lo justo. Quisiéramos ir el sábado 14 de noviembre.
reply:
¡Con mucho gusto! 🐠 Y tranqui, es súper normal sentir esos nervios la primera vez — el instructor va con ustedes todo el tiempo.

Sobre la profundidad: en el minicurso se baja hasta 12 metros máximo, pero lo habitual es entre 5 y 12 metros. Se va a la profundidad que cada uno maneje con comodidad, siempre respetando ese límite.

Y lo de nadar: no hace falta ser un delfín 😄. El minicurso está pensado justo para principiantes, con práctica previa en piscina y el instructor pendiente de ustedes en todo momento. Eso sí, para el formulario médico y cualquier detalle puntual de salud, lo mejor es que lo mire un asesor del equipo.

Sobre el sábado 14 de noviembre: ¡de una! Buceamos todos los días del año (solo cerramos el 25 de diciembre y el 1 de enero), así que esa fecha está perfecta. La eliges en el calendario al momento de reservar.

Un par de cosas importantes para el minicurso:
- Hay que llenar el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol
- No hay teoría previa: se hace allí mismo, el mismo día, con el instructor
- Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 12 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
- Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda (el equipo va incluido)

También necesitas:
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.

Como son colombianos, el pago en pesos lo coordina un asesor al cerrar la reserva, al mismo precio online. 😊

🤿 *Minicurso de Buceo*
💰 *655.000 COP* por persona · 2 personas

El pago es en pesos colombianos (COP): pueden pagar *100 % online* o un *anticipo del 50 %* con el enlace, el QR o Llave que envía el asesor, y el *otro 50 % el día de la actividad*.

Ten en cuenta que el minicurso es una iniciación de un día y no certifica; para certificarte está el curso Open Water (2 días, con noche en las islas).

msg: Solo yo. Voy con las dos salidas de un día entonces. ¿Cómo hago para que me apliquen el 5 % si reservo por la web? ¿Y a qué profundidad y en qué sitios se bucea? Me interesa saber si hay algo más profundo, tipo 25 o 30 metros, porque tengo el Advanced.
reply:
¡De una! Con tu Advanced puedes llegar hasta 30 metros, así que sí hay opción de bucear profundo. La profundidad real de cada inmersión depende del punto que se elija ese día, siempre respetando el máximo de tu titulación. En las Islas del Rosario tenemos sitios con diferentes perfiles, y el guía arma el plan según el nivel del grupo y las condiciones del día. Los nombres puntuales de los sitios no los tengo a la mano, pero eso te lo detalla el instructor en la lancha. 🐠

Sobre el 5% por tu equipo completo: no hay código ni casilla en la web para eso. Lo que haces es reservar y pagar online (ahí ya te entra el 10% automático), y el 5% de equipo propio lo aplica el equipo. Como es un descuento que hay que pedir antes de pagar, lo mejor es que reserves por el link y le escribas al equipo para que te lo ajusten. Te dejo el link de la salida de 2 inmersiones desde Cartagena: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/salidas-de-buceo/1?language=es

Ahí eliges la fecha y las personas, y pagas con tarjeta (con pasaporte como documento). Recuerda que son dos reservas, una para el 27 y otra para el 28 de noviembre.

Quien no es colombiano ni residente en Colombia paga en dólares (USD) con tarjeta en la web; la tarifa es la misma, solo cambia la moneda.

Te recomiendo el plan de *2 inmersiones en 1 día* en las Islas del Rosario. (Si prefieres más inmersiones, hay *paquetes* de 3 o más; dímelo.)

¿Han pasado *más de 2 años* desde tu última inmersión?

msg: Hola, buenos días. Soy Diana, de Bogotá. Quiero sacarme la certificación de buceo y he pensado hacerlo en Cartagena en enero. Tengo asma leve, controlada con inhalador, y hace años que no tengo una crisis. ¿Puedo hacer el curso igual? ¿Cuánto dura y cuánto cuesta?
reply:
¡Hola Diana, bienvenida! 🐠 Qué chévere que quieras sacar tu certificación, es una experiencia hermosa y las Islas del Rosario son un lugar espectacular para hacerlo.

Sobre el curso: el Curso Básico PADI (Open Water) dura 2 días. El día 1 empiezas con la teoría online (PADI eLearning, unas 10-12 horas que haces antes) y luego en las islas piscina + 2 inmersiones; el día 2 son 2 inmersiones más y el trámite de la certificación. Te certifica para bucear hasta 18 m.

Ojo con un detalle: este curso requiere dormir al menos una noche en las islas (la del día 1), el alojamiento no está incluido y se reserva directo con el hotel.

Precio por persona: 2.450.000 COP online (2.722.000 COP normal).

Y sobre el asma, eso lo evalúa una persona del equipo con el formulario médico antes de la actividad.

Para preguntas médicas específicas, es importante que hables con nuestro staff calificado para evaluar tu situación particular. Te paso ahora con alguien del equipo, que te escribe por aquí enseguida.

Políticas de Diving Planet:
- Esperar al menos 18 horas para tomar un avión después de buceo recreativo. 12 horas mínimo después del minicurso (solo para quien no está certificado). El refresher también son 18 horas: es para buzos certificados, aunque se reserve como el minicurso. Las horas se cuentan desde la última inmersión, no desde la vuelta a Cartagena. La inmersión del minicurso termina hacia las 12:00 (mediodía): sus 12 horas se cuentan desde ahí. Si la última inmersión es de día, también la del refresher (las actividades acaban hacia las 12:00-13:00), se puede volar desde las 7:00 a. m. del día siguiente; tras el minicurso, desde la medianoche de ese mismo día. Si la última es nocturna, las horas se cuentan desde ella. Un vuelo al día siguiente a las 7:00 a. m. o más tarde SÍ llega: se puede bucear el día anterior, y la hora de vuelta a Cartagena de ese día no cambia nada. Para un buzo certificado, un vuelo el MISMO día de la inmersión NUNCA llega, sea a la hora que sea, también por la noche: con un vuelo el domingo por la noche, la última inmersión tiene que ser como muy tarde el sábado; que la lancha vuelva antes de irse no lo arregla. Quien dice que se va ese día sin decir cómo, probablemente vuela: dile esto. Al contestar, di primero desde qué hora puede volar y después compáralo con su vuelo; no empieces por sí o no.
- Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh; los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) los revisa un asesor del equipo. Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente. El refresher es el minicurso (piscina y una inmersión con instructor) y ocupa su propio día: ese mismo día no se hace la salida de buceo. Quien viene varios días hace el refresher el primero y bucea los demás.
- Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.
- Muelle de la Bodeguita, a 5 minutos del centro histórico, a las 8:00 AM. Saliendo desde Cartagena no hay recogida en el hotel: cada persona llega por su cuenta al muelle (el transporte terrestre hasta el muelle no está incluido).
- Al reservar aceptas nuestros términos y condiciones, política de cancelación y tratamiento de datos personales. Ver: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Los cambios de fecha están sujetos a disponibilidad y a nuestros términos y condiciones. Ver: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Los cambios en el número de personas de una reserva ya hecha están sujetos a disponibilidad y a nuestros términos y condiciones. Ver: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Pagan en pesos colombianos (COP) los colombianos (quien tiene la nacionalidad colombiana, con cédula o pasaporte colombiano, viva donde viva; también con doble nacionalidad, si una es la colombiana) y los residentes en Colombia (quien tiene cédula de extranjería, que es un documento de residente; vivir en Colombia sin ella no basta). Decir que es colombiano o de una ciudad de Colombia ("soy de Cali") ya lo dice; lo que no basta es solo haber nacido allí viviendo fuera: entonces se le pregunta si tiene la nacionalidad colombiana o cédula de extranjería. El resto de clientes internacionales paga en dólares (USD). Un grupo no se paga por partes: si en la misma reserva hay colombianos o residentes y también extranjeros sin cédula de extranjería, todo el grupo paga en dólares (USD), también los residentes y los colombianos. Un colombiano con quien tiene cédula de extranjería, sea de donde sea, no es un grupo mixto: pagan los dos en pesos (COP). El precio es el mismo: solo cambia la moneda (no hay descuento por ser colombiano).
- Si en el grupo hay colombianos o residentes y también extranjeros sin cédula de extranjería, toda la reserva del grupo se paga en dólares (USD), al mismo precio equivalente. Quien tiene cédula de extranjería no cuenta como extranjero, sea de donde sea. No hay un precio distinto por ser colombiano.
- Si ya estás en las Islas del Rosario, coordinamos recogida y regreso desde hoteles con acceso marítimo. En algunos casos la lancha llega directo al hotel; en otros te indicamos el muelle o punto más cercano.
- Estos planes manejan precios diferentes porque no incluyen transporte desde Cartagena ni almuerzo.
- La recogida es solo en las Islas del Rosario: Barú (también Playa Blanca, que está en Barú) no es parte de las islas y allí no operamos ni recogemos; quien se aloja en Barú sale desde Cartagena (Muelle de la Bodeguita).
- Depende de la actividad: snorkeling desde los 6 años; Bubble Makers de 8 a 10 años (minicurso en piscina y aguas poco profundas, máx. 2 metros); minicurso de buceo y curso Open Water desde los 10 años; Curso Avanzado (Advanced) y curso Rescue desde los 12. - No se permite llevar ni tomar alcohol en la lancha ni durante la actividad, y no se puede consumir alcohol u otras sustancias antes de bucear. Debes presentarte en buen estado físico.
- El sistema de reservas de la página web. Se cierra automáticamente a las 4:30 PM del día anterior: pasada esa hora ya no se puede reservar para el día siguiente, y se reserva igual por la web para el siguiente día disponible.
- Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.

Desde las islas: recogida en el hotel entre las 9:30 y las 9:45 (a las 8:00 en las especialidades y a las 7:30 el día 2 de algunos cursos). Sistema de reservas online cierra a las 4:30 p.m. del día anterior; pasada esa hora se reserva por la web para el siguiente día disponible.
- Solo cerramos el 25 de diciembre y el 1 de enero. El resto del año operamos todos los días, incluyendo festivos, salvo suspensión por condiciones meteorológicas adversas.
- El tour incluye agua todo el día, dulces de coco entre inmersiones y almuerzo (arroz con pollo o arroz con vegetales). El menú es siempre el mismo, no cambia según día/proveedor. Vegetarianos, veganos y celíacos reciben arroz con vegetales. El cliente puede llevar su propia comida si lo necesita (ej. alergia o dieta especial). Si el cliente tiene alguna alergia alimentaria, debe informarnos antes del tour. En los paquetes de varios días saliendo desde Cartagena el almuerzo va incluido solo el primer día; en los planes de quien ya está en las islas no se incluye almuerzo.

Vale para todas las actividades, también el minicurso (y el refresher, que se reserva como minicurso), los cursos PADI y las salidas de buzos certificados: no incluidas, el instructor puede hacerlas voluntariamente.

Se aceptan: discapacidad auditiva (sordos), discapacidad visual (ciegos), movilidad reducida (silla de ruedas), Síndrome de Down, Parálisis Cerebral y Autismo (según nivel y evaluación). Todos los instructores están formados en buceo adaptado. Se recomienda avisar con anticipación. La limitación es la presencia de condiciones médicas adicionales que contraindiquen el buceo.
- Si ya estás en las Islas del Rosario y tu hotel tiene acceso marítimo, la recogida y el regreso en lancha están incluidos sin cargo adicional.
- Buceamos en las Islas del Rosario, dentro del Parque Nacional Natural Corales del Rosario y San Bernardo, a unos 45-60 minutos en lancha desde Cartagena.
- Todas las actividades de día (salidas de buceo, minicurso, snorkel, cursos y cada día de los paquetes) terminan hacia las 12:00-13:00, y después viene la comida. Quien sale desde Cartagena tiene el almuerzo incluido en las islas y la lancha regresa a Cartagena a las 3:00 p.m. (llegada aprox. 4:15 p.m.); quien está alojado en las islas vuelve a su hotel hacia las 12:00-13:00 a comer (almuerzo no incluido). - Las actividades y los cursos se dan en español y en inglés. Si un participante no habla ninguno de los dos idiomas, puede venir con alguien que le haga de intérprete, pero la instrucción sigue siendo en español o en inglés.
- Se reserva por la página web, en el enlace de cada actividad (con el 10% de descuento online). Es igual saliendo desde Cartagena o ya en las islas: no hay teoría online ni por correo; la teoría se hace allí, el mismo día, junto con la práctica en piscina y 1 inmersión en el mar con instructor.
- Los clientes extranjeros pagan el 100 % con tarjeta en la página web; con una tarjeta extranjera se usa el pasaporte como documento de identificación.
- Los colombianos y los residentes en Colombia (también quien tiene cédula de extranjería) pagan en pesos y no usan el enlace de reserva de la web: la reserva siempre la cierra un asesor del equipo por este chat, que les envía el enlace, el QR o Llave para pagar el 100 % online o un anticipo del 50 %, y el otro 50 % el día de la actividad, con tarjeta o efectivo. Para reservar para el día siguiente hay que hacerlo antes de las 4:30 p. m. del día anterior.
- Quien paga en dólares reserva y paga por el enlace online: el pago se registra al momento y el equipo lo concilia poco después para confirmar la reserva; solo si falla el pago online el equipo envía un enlace para pagar por transferencia.
- Si el sistema de reservas o el pago en línea falla, el equipo te envía un link para pagar por transferencia, y se mantiene el 10 % de descuento online (porque falló el online). Fuera de ese caso no se paga por transferencia: el descuento del 10 % es por reservar y pagar online.
- En los grupos que combinan buceo y snorkel, el snorkel se hace en una zona distinta a la del buceo. Si hay poca gente van juntos en la misma lancha; si no, se dividen por actividad.

- Para reservar una actividad saliendo desde las islas, el cliente tiene que tener ya su hotel y decirnos cuál: la recogida se coordina allí. Si todavía no lo tiene, primero reserva el hotel y nos escribe con el nombre; entonces reservamos. Si reservara antes la actividad, podrían cancelarle el hotel, podría no quedar sitio, podría olvidarse de avisarnos o acabar saliendo desde Cartagena. Si se aloja en una casa, un Airbnb o un hotel fuera de nuestra lista, nos dice el nombre y un asesor le confirma la recogida antes de reservar y pagar: no se reserva hasta entonces.

- Los horarios de salida y de recogida son fijos: no se pueden adelantar ni retrasar. Si necesitas un ajuste, lo revisa un asesor del equipo.
- Las cancelaciones por mal clima son poco probables porque las Islas del Rosario están en aguas protegidas. Si la Capitanía de Puerto cierra las salidas hacia las islas, primero se intenta reprogramar la actividad para que no pierdas tu reserva. Si no es posible reagendar, se realiza un reembolso del 100%. Consulta los términos y condiciones: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/

- Si te mareas en la lancha (el trayecto a las islas es de aproximadamente 1 hora en lancha rápida): desayuna ligero antes de salir y considera pastillas para el mareo. Si tomas alguna medicación, consulta con tu médico si puedes bucear con ella.

- Los grupos son reducidos y siguen los estándares de seguridad de PADI en cada actividad.
- La lancha es una lancha normal y no tiene baño. En las islas se usan las instalaciones del hotel donde se almuerza: ahí se cambian, usan el baño y se duchan.

- No hay tarjeta regalo, pero se puede reservar a nombre de otra persona; la fecha y los detalles se coordinan con un asesor.
- No se fuma en la lancha.

- Los bebés y los niños pequeños que todavía no tienen edad para ninguna actividad (el snorkel es desde los 6 años) pueden ir en la lancha con sus padres, a cualquier edad, y no pagan.

Políticas de Diving Planet:
- Esperar al menos 18 horas para tomar un avión después de buceo recreativo. 12 horas mínimo después del minicurso (solo para quien no está certificado). El refresher también son 18 horas: es para buzos certificados, aunque se reserve como el minicurso. Las horas se cuentan desde la última inmersión, no desde la vuelta a Cartagena. La inmersión del minicurso termina hacia las 12:00 (mediodía): sus 12 horas se cuentan desde ahí. Si la última inmersión es de día, también la del refresher (las actividades acaban hacia las 12:00-13:00), se puede volar desde las 7:00 a. m. del día siguiente; tras el minicurso, desde la medianoche de ese mismo día. Si la última es nocturna, las horas se cuentan desde ella. Un vuelo al día siguiente a las 7:00 a. m. o más tarde SÍ llega: se puede bucear el día anterior, y la hora de vuelta a Cartagena de ese día no cambia nada. Para un buzo certificado, un vuelo el MISMO día de la inmersión NUNCA llega, sea a la hora que sea, también por la noche: con un vuelo el domingo por la noche, la última inmersión tiene que ser como muy tarde el sábado; que la lancha vuelva antes de irse no lo arregla. Quien dice que se va ese día sin decir cómo, probablemente vuela: dile esto. Al contestar, di primero desde qué hora puede volar y después compáralo con su vuelo; no empieces por sí o no.
- Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh; los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) los revisa un asesor del equipo. Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente. El refresher es el minicurso (piscina y una inmersión con instructor) y ocupa su propio día: ese mismo día no se hace la salida de buceo. Quien viene varios días hace el refresher el primero y bucea los demás.
- Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.
- Muelle de la Bodeguita, a 5 minutos del centro histórico, a las 8:00 AM. Saliendo desde Cartagena no hay recogida en el hotel: cada persona llega por su cuenta al muelle (el transporte terrestre hasta el muelle no está incluido).
- Al reservar aceptas nuestros términos y condiciones, política de cancelación y tratamiento de datos personales. Ver: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Los cambios de fecha están sujetos a disponibilidad y a nuestros términos y condiciones. Ver: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Los cambios en el número de personas de una reserva ya hecha están sujetos a disponibilidad y a nuestros términos y condiciones. Ver: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Pagan en pesos colombianos (COP) los colombianos (quien tiene la nacionalidad colombiana, con cédula o pasaporte colombiano, viva donde viva; también con doble nacionalidad, si una es la colombiana) y los residentes en Colombia (quien tiene cédula de extranjería, que es un documento de residente; vivir en Colombia sin ella no basta). Decir que es colombiano o de una ciudad de Colombia ("soy de Cali") ya lo dice; lo que no basta es solo haber nacido allí viviendo fuera: entonces se le pregunta si tiene la nacionalidad colombiana o cédula de extranjería. El resto de clientes internacionales paga en dólares (USD). Un grupo no se paga por partes: si en la misma reserva hay colombianos o residentes y también extranjeros sin cédula de extranjería, todo el grupo paga en dólares (USD), también los residentes y los colombianos. Un colombiano con quien tiene cédula de extranjería, sea de donde sea, no es un grupo mixto: pagan los dos en pesos (COP). El precio es el mismo: solo cambia la moneda (no hay descuento por ser colombiano).
- Si en el grupo hay colombianos o residentes y también extranjeros sin cédula de extranjería, toda la reserva del grupo se paga en dólares (USD), al mismo precio equivalente. Quien tiene cédula de extranjería no cuenta como extranjero, sea de donde sea. No hay un precio distinto por ser colombiano.
- Si ya estás en las Islas del Rosario, coordinamos recogida y regreso desde hoteles con acceso marítimo. En algunos casos la lancha llega directo al hotel; en otros te indicamos el muelle o punto más cercano.
- Estos planes manejan precios diferentes porque no incluyen transporte desde Cartagena ni almuerzo.
- La recogida es solo en las Islas del Rosario: Barú (también Playa Blanca, que está en Barú) no es parte de las islas y allí no operamos ni recogemos; quien se aloja en Barú sale desde Cartagena (Muelle de la Bodeguita).
- Depende de la actividad: snorkeling desde los 6 años; Bubble Makers de 8 a 10 años (minicurso en piscina y aguas poco profundas, máx. 2 metros); minicurso de buceo y curso Open Water desde los 10 años; Curso Avanzado (Advanced) y curso Rescue desde los 12. Menores de edad deben estar acompañados por un padre o pariente responsable demostrable.

- No se permite llevar ni tomar alcohol en la lancha ni durante la actividad, y no se puede consumir alcohol u otras sustancias antes de bucear. Debes presentarte en buen estado físico.
- El sistema de reservas de la página web. Se cierra automáticamente a las 4:30 PM del día anterior: pasada esa hora ya no se puede reservar para el día siguiente, y se reserva igual por la web para el siguiente día disponible.
- Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
- Desde Cartagena: salida a las 8:00 a.m. desde el Muelle de la Bodeguita y regreso a las 3:00 p.m. (llegada aprox. 4:15 p.m.). Desde las islas: recogida en el hotel entre las 9:30 y las 9:45 (a las 8:00 en las especialidades y a las 7:30 el día 2 de algunos cursos). Las actividades de día terminan hacia las 12:00-13:00 (ver el horario de las actividades). Buceo nocturno: por la tarde-noche (recogida hacia las 5:30 p.m. y regreso hacia las 7:30 p.m.). Sistema de reservas online cierra a las 4:30 p.m. del día anterior; pasada esa hora se reserva por la web para el siguiente día disponible.
- Solo cerramos el 25 de diciembre y el 1 de enero. El resto del año operamos todos los días, incluyendo festivos, salvo suspensión por condiciones meteorológicas adversas.
- El tour incluye agua todo el día, dulces de coco entre inmersiones y almuerzo (arroz con pollo o arroz con vegetales). El menú es siempre el mismo, no cambia según día/proveedor. Vegetarianos, veganos y celíacos reciben arroz con vegetales. El cliente puede llevar su propia comida si lo necesita (ej. alergia o dieta especial). Si el cliente tiene alguna alergia alimentaria, debe informarnos antes del tour. En los paquetes de varios días saliendo desde Cartagena el almuerzo va incluido solo el primer día; en los planes de quien ya está en las islas no se incluye almuerzo.

Vale para todas las actividades, también el minicurso (y el refresher, que se reserva como minicurso), los cursos PADI y las salidas de buzos certificados: no incluidas, el instructor puede hacerlas voluntariamente.

Lo mismo en los paquetes de buceo de varios días (4, 5, 7 y 9 inmersiones): se duerme en las islas y el alojamiento, que no está incluido, se reserva directamente con el hotel.

Se aceptan: discapacidad auditiva (sordos), discapacidad visual (ciegos), movilidad reducida (silla de ruedas), Síndrome de Down, Parálisis Cerebral y Autismo (según nivel y evaluación). Todos los instructores están formados en buceo adaptado. Se recomienda avisar con anticipación. La limitación es la presencia de condiciones médicas adicionales que contraindiquen el buceo.
- Si ya estás en las Islas del Rosario y tu hotel tiene acceso marítimo, la recogida y el regreso en lancha están incluidos sin cargo adicional.
- Buceamos en las Islas del Rosario, dentro del Parque Nacional Natural Corales del Rosario y San Bernardo, a unos 45-60 minutos en lancha desde Cartagena.
- Todas las actividades de día (salidas de buceo, minicurso, snorkel, cursos y cada día de los paquetes) terminan hacia las 12:00-13:00, y después viene la comida. Quien sale desde Cartagena tiene el almuerzo incluido en las islas y la lancha regresa a Cartagena a las 3:00 p.m. (llegada aprox. 4:15 p.m.); quien está alojado en las islas vuelve a su hotel hacia las 12:00-13:00 a comer (almuerzo no incluido). - Las actividades y los cursos se dan en español y en inglés. Si un participante no habla ninguno de los dos idiomas, puede venir con alguien que le haga de intérprete, pero la instrucción sigue siendo en español o en inglés.
- Se reserva por la página web, en el enlace de cada actividad (con el 10% de descuento online).
